teachingQuestion: How does a security risk become an accountable business decision?
focalInsight: Security analysis informs the decision, but authorized leadership owns direction and residual-risk acceptance while oversight receives evidence.
title: From business objective to accountable risk decision
caption: Decision rights, implementation, and oversight are separate jobs connected by evidence.
altSummary: A five-step flow shows business objectives setting context, security analysis informing an authorized owner, management operating controls, and governance reviewing evidence.
textFallback: Business objectives and obligations set context. Security analysis provides options and residual-risk evidence. An authorized owner chooses a treatment or acceptance. Management implements and measures controls. Governance oversight reviews evidence and requires adjustment, keeping the cycle aligned with business objectives.
